report.summary: Chunk 2 of 11: defines three feature gates (documents, types, wiki) and their env vars, plus _collect_docs helper; extensive comments explain design rationale.

claims.text: The moment forest.py reads type_nodes, a type-bearing index produces a forest with more nodes, more relation layers and therefore a DIFFERENT content_sha256.
claims.why: forest.py and content_sha256 are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: per-file EXTRACTION is unconditional (see perfile.FileAnalysis.type_facts).

claims.text: Gating extraction would put the flag on the wrong side of a content-keyed disk cache and a layer-off row would be served as a hit to a layer-on build -- an empty type block with no error.
claims.why: Cache mechanism not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: What the gate covers is whole-repo RESOLUTION (serial, in the parent, not cached) and PUBLICATION.
claims.why: Resolution and publication functions not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Because the gate changes the returned dict, it is part of _scope_key exactly as documents is.
claims.why: _scope_key not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Type nodes are excluded, always, from: modules (so also hotspots / module_heat / score_modules), import_edges / import_edges_reverse / dependencies / fan_in, graph._graph_nodes (the fence's denominator), all_units and therefore all four clone passes, and graph.build_resolver's defs_by_file.
claims.why: Those symbols are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Their relations live in their own layer, type_edges.
claims.why: type_edges not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: types_enabled: Whether this build resolves and publishes the type layer. Explicit argument wins; else the DAEDALUS_INDEX_TYPES env var; else False.
claims.why: Implementation checks flag first, then env var, then returns False implicitly.

claims.text: WIKI. markdown.py parses [[wikilinks]] and resolves doc->doc and doc->code, but until this gate existed nothing called knowledge_links -- the parser had no consumer, which is the same defect skills.py had for a thousand lines.
claims.why: markdown.py and skills.py not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Gated for the same reason documents and types are: turning it on adds edges, and an edge set that changes without a deliberate act is how a ranking moves for a reason nobody can name.
claims.why: No edge set or ranking logic in this chunk.

claims.text: document_links is NOT touched by this. That block is built from internal_links exactly as before, so an index built without this flag is byte-identical to one built before the flag existed.
claims.why: document_links and internal_links not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: wiki_enabled: Whether this build resolves and publishes the wiki link layer. Explicit argument wins; else DAEDALUS_INDEX_WIKI; else False.
claims.why: Implementation checks flag first, then env var, then returns False implicitly.

claims.text: A separate walk rather than a second return value from _collect: _collect's (root, max_files) -> list signature is monkeypatched by tests/test_structcore_parallel.py to prove walk-order independence, and widening it would break that proof for a saving of one os.walk (~0.2s on a 7k-file tree, and only when documents are enabled at all).
claims.why: _collect function and test file not present in this chunk.

observations.what: All three gate functions follow the same pattern: explicit argument first, then env var, default False.
The _collect_docs function is incomplete: it uses doc_spec_for which is not defined in this chunk.
The _collect_docs function uses _IGNORE_DIRS which is not defined in this chunk.
The _collect_docs function returns early if max_files is reached, but does not handle the case where max_files is negative or zero.
The claim about ~0.2s saving on a 7k-file tree is an estimate and cannot be verified from this code.
